paper_metadata.title: Variational Quantum Factorization (VQF) using Different Variations of Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA)

summary: The paper studies variational quantum factorization of 143, 291311, and 175 using four QAOA variants on the Qiskit simulation framework: standard QAOA, maQAOA, CVaR QAOA, and CVaR maQAOA. The best reported success probabilities are 0.92 for 143, 0.56 for 291311, and 0.99 for 175, with maQAOA or CVaR maQAOA performing best; no classical baseline or practical quantum advantage is demonstrated.

experiments.description: Variational quantum factorization of 143, 291311, and 175 using standard QAOA, multi-angle QAOA, CVaR QAOA, and CVaR multi-angle QAOA on Qiskit simulation.

algorithm.variant: standard QAOA; multi-angle QAOA (maQAOA); CVaR QAOA; CVaR maQAOA
algorithm.ansatz: QAOA layered ansatz with Hadamard initialization, problem-unitary Uc, and mixer-unitary UM

hyperparameters.alpha: CVaR fraction; values reported include 1 and 0.75

algorithm.parameter_initialization: initial superposition state |+>^n via Hadamard gates; variational parameters not otherwise specified

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Binary variables represent factor bits; mapped to qubits via ak -> (I - sigma_z)/2; 1 qubit per binary variable
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize sum of squared simplified factorization clauses; for 143, reduced objective includes up to 3-body terms and is encoded as an Ising Hamiltonian
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Implicit via penalty/objective construction from factorization clauses; CVaR changes expectation evaluation, not feasibility constraints
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: For 143: Hc = -sigma_z0 sigma_z1 sigma_z2 /4 + sigma_z0 sigma_z1 /4 + 3 sigma_z0 sigma_z2 /4 + sigma_z0 sigma_z3 /4 + sigma_z0 /2 - sigma_z1 sigma_z2 sigma_z3 /4 - sigma_z1 sigma_z2 /4 + 3 sigma_z1 sigma_z3 /4 + sigma_z1 /4 + sigma_z2 sigma_z3 /4 + sigma_z2 /4 + sigma_z3 /2 + 2

problem_instance.description: Factorization of bi-prime numbers 143 and 291311, and tri-prime number 175
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Binary multiplication clauses simplified using Anschuetz et al. rules; then mapped to Ising form
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Success probability measured from sampled bitstrings; highest success probability reported across QAOA depth p and alpha settings

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Factorization clauses derived from binary multiplication and simplified before Hamiltonian construction
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: From measured bitstrings, factors are reconstructed and success counted when product equals target number

speedup_claims.caveats: No classical baseline or speedup comparison is reported; the paper only compares QAOA variants against each other.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Shor-related motivation discussed; no asymptotic complexity for QAOA VQF given
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Best classical approximation algorithm works in sub-exponential time to factorize the same number

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: No classical baseline comparison is reported; the paper only compares standard QAOA, maQAOA, CVaR QAOA, and CVaR maQAOA on Qiskit simulation.
limiting_factors: No classical baseline or runtime comparison
Problem sizes are small-to-moderate factorization instances (143, 175, 291311)
Success probability is the only reported performance metric

notes: hardware.type inferred as simulator_other because the paper states Qiskit quantum simulation framework and no real QPU is named.

num_qubits inferred from the factorization encodings: 143 uses 4 qubits, 291311 uses 6 qubits, and 175 uses 3 qubits; the paper does not present a single unified qubit count for the combined experiment.
The paper reports only relative performance among QAOA variants, not against a classical factoring baseline.
Highest reported success probabilities are 0.92 for 143, 0.56 for 291311, and 0.99 for 175.
